clue.text: Play another simple game

indicators.note: game in the sense of willing or lame suggests the preceding words are up for being knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone suggests playing yet another easy game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is the anagram signal on ANOTHER SIMPLE, whose thirteen letters rearrange into the title of Molière's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière's 1666 comedy about a man who despises society is a stage play.

clue.text: Misplace a treatment for antenatal condition

indicators.note: treatment, a working over, says the letters before it are reprocessed

explanation.surface: Getting a treatment wrong for a condition in pregnancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges MISPLACEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A dangerous pregnancy disorder of seizures and high blood pressure is an antenatal condition.

clue.text: Dramatist heading off to place underground

indicators.note: heading off says the dramatist loses his first letter

parts.note: Harold Pinter, the British playwright

explanation.surface: A playwright sets off for somewhere below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the P from PINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, putting something in the ground.

clue.text: Leaderless demo in some leaderless state?

indicators.note: in places the shortened demo inside the word for some

parts.note: some can mean any

indicators.note: Leaderless says the demonstration loses its first letter

parts.note: a demo, a protest, is a march

explanation.surface: A demonstration without a leader in some state with no leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' appears twice: first it beheads the demo, then it sits in the definition, a state with no ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A state with no ruler or government is in anarchy.

clue.text: Article about country girl

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about or concerning
SA is South Africa

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a country girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a female first name, the girl of the clue.

clue.text: Liars Cameron's right about

indicators.note: about, in the sense of turned around, says these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician's right-wing colleagues are called liars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CAMERONS with R.
explanation.definitionFit: People who romance, telling fanciful untrue stories, are fabricators.

clue.text: Show love for English militant

indicators.note: love for English says the zero replaces the E

parts.note: to show is to prove
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Show how much you love an English activist.
explanation.walkthrough: In PROVE, O (love) replaces E (English).
explanation.definitionFit: Provo is a nickname for a member of the Provisional IRA, a militant.

clue.text: "Noted drama as Princess Elizabeth initially escaped with the Queen Mother" (the Guardian)

parts.note: Princess Diana, known as Di

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Elizabeth

parts.note: fled means escaped
ER, Elizabeth Regina
ma is mother
the newspaper speaking of itself is us

explanation.surface: A mock tabloid headline about royal women fleeing, attributed to the paper itself.
explanation.walkthrough: '(the Guardian)' supplies US because the clue is the newspaper talking about itself; 'Noted' hints at musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Strauss's operetta The Bat is a drama set to music, hence noted.

clue.text: Show off bare legs? I'm no good wearing not so much

indicators.note: wearing means the smaller amount is put on around the rest

parts.note: less means not so much

indicators.note: off means the letters of bare legs and I'm go astray

explanation.surface: Should I show off bare legs? I'm not so good in less clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show off' looks like a phrase, but 'Show' is the definition and 'off' the anagram signal; 'no good' drops a G and 'wearing' wraps the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running Boublil and Schönberg musical is a West End show.

clue.text: Embarrassed by bisexuality of the Italian guy

parts.note: Italian 'the' in both genders: masculine IL and feminine LA
to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: Someone is flustered by an Italian man's bisexuality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bisexuality' is a playful way of asking for both the male and female forms of the Italian definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling uncomfortable and awkward is a common idiom for being embarrassed.

clue.text: African 14 for World Cup winning captain

parts.note: a Moor is a North African of Berber or Arab descent
14 across is ECSTASY, the drug, abbreviated as E

explanation.surface: An African player is put in place of a captain who lifted the World Cup.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 14 across, whose answer is commonly shortened to E.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby Moore captained England when they won the football World Cup in 1966.

clue.text: Drink lower-class female knocked back, showing a bit of leg

indicators.note: knocked back, as a drink is downed, also tells us the three pieces run in reverse order

parts.note: rum is a spirit drunk
E is the lowest social grade in the British ABCDE classification

explanation.surface: A working-class woman downs her drink, showing a bit of leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses RUM E F as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh bone is the main bone of the upper leg, so it is part of a leg.

clue.text: Swimming pool without running water — Cameron's controlled environment

indicators.note: swimming, as in a head that swims, signals the letters are jumbled
without means the following piece is taken away from pool

parts.note: the Po is a river in Italy, running water
David Cameron's name taken as written

explanation.surface: A swimming pool with no running water is Prime Minister Cameron's controlled environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes PO from POOL, leaving OL; 'Swimming' rearranges OL with CAMERON.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean room is a sealed workspace with filtered air, a controlled environment for making microchips and the like.

clue.text: First of actors leaving company in simple form of transport

indicators.note: in places the shortened company inside the word for simple

parts.note: simple means easy

indicators.note: leaving says the picked letter departs from the company

parts.note: the cast of a play is its company of actors

indicators.note: First of picks the opening letter of actors

explanation.surface: An actor quits the company, finding it a simple way to get carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' here means rapture, not a vehicle, and 'simple' gives the container rather than describing the transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is a transport of delight, a crossword sense of transport as rapture.

clue.text: Strongly confident "Hair" topped in 20 down on the rise

indicators.note: on the rise in a down clue means the assembled letters are read upwards
in places the trimmed hair inside the musical

parts.note: 20 down is a stage musical, here the Lloyd Webber show Evita

indicators.note: topped means the hair loses its top letter

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: The hit musical Hair is outdone by another musical whose popularity is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' cuts TRESS to RESS, 'in' puts it in EVITA to give EVITRESSA, and 'on the rise' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Assertive behaviour is forthright and self-assured, strongly confident.

clue.text: Info hidden in girl's to-do lists

indicators.note: hidden in puts the information piece inside the girl's name

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name, with its possessive S
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Information is tucked away in a girl's lists of jobs to do.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Lists of things to be done at a meeting or in a day are agendas.

clue.text: Ruffian of the French party, carrying out rape

indicators.note: carrying means the French words and party hold the rest within them

parts.note: des means of the in French
a do is a party

indicators.note: out, as in put out of shape, signals that rape is anagrammed

explanation.surface: A French ruffian at a party commits a violent assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' makes the French article and the party a single outer case around the scrambled assault, with 'out' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw or bandit, a ruffian.

clue.text: Passes through part of church in the Spanish quarter

indicators.note: in places the church part within the Spanish article and quarter

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: Someone walks through part of a church in the Spanish quarter of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' is a compass point here, S, not a district.
explanation.definitionFit: Time passes or goes by is the same as saying it slips away, the verb's usual sense.

clue.text: Ray means business — ultimately starts reconditioned old car

indicators.note: reconditioned, like an engine overhauled, says the letters are rebuilt in a new order
starts picks the opening letters of business and ultimately

explanation.surface: Ray means business when he restores a vintage car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' gives B and U, which 'reconditioned' rearranges with MEANS. Sunbeam was a British car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam of sunlight is a ray, and the Sunbeam was a British motor car.

clue.text: Wrongly surmise one's made a poor application

indicators.note: wrongly tells us the next word is set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone guessing wrongly turns out to have made a poor job application.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' stands for 'one who has', so the definition describes a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has applied something badly or abused it is one who puts it to wrong use.

clue.text: First of 21 exactly as written in standard non-American description of 9

indicators.note: First of picks the opening letter of the answer to 21

parts.note: 21 across is the answer to that clue

indicators.note: in places the Latin word inside the shortened standard
non-American removes the abbreviation for America

parts.note: usual means standard or normal
sic is the Latin tag marking a quotation exactly as written

explanation.surface: A precise, unamerican description of the subject of clue 9.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-American' strips the US abbreviation from standard, and the Latin tag SIC, used in quotations, sits inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Misérables is a stage show with songs, the genre that describes it.

clue.text: Errors of the type seen in road runs

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
sprints are short fast runs

explanation.surface: Mistakes in printing turn up in road races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the type' points to printing type, not a kind of error.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistakes made in setting printed type are typographical slips.

clue.text: Mug a German at end of short road

indicators.note: at end of places the German word after the road

parts.note: St is short for street
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Someone mugs a German at the end of a short road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is a noun, a beer mug, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large German beer mug.

clue.text: An Eastern European said to be bitter

indicators.note: said tells us the eastern European is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a Serb is a native of Serbia in the Balkans

explanation.surface: An Eastern European is said to be resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Serb' and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour or harsh in taste or temper; acerbic is the more familiar form.

clue.text: Emitting light from silver base

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
base means low

explanation.surface: Light gleams from a silver base.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing, shining with warmth, means emitting light.

clue.text: Somewhat reflecting desire: tumescent organs

indicators.note: reflecting says the hidden letters are read backwards
Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A risqué line about desire making certain organs swell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' takes IRETU from 'desire: tumescent' and 'reflecting' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombs are reproductive organs; the Latin plural of the word for womb.

clue.text: Give absolution to former copper with 50p to broadcast 8

parts.note: ex means former
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
L is the Roman numeral for 50 and p is pence

indicators.note: broadcast means the number is heard over the air, so only its sound counts

parts.note: the number eight

explanation.surface: A former policeman with 50 pence has to broadcast an absolution to 8 down.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' is the number here, not the cross-reference to 8 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To exculpate is to clear of blame, close to absolving someone of guilt.

clue.text: Great work setting for which bugger all returns

definitions.text: Great work setting for which bugger all returns

parts.words: Great work setting for which bugger all returns
parts.note: a celebrated Welsh radio play whose village setting, Llareggub, is the phrase 'bugger all' written backwards

explanation.surface: A masterpiece of a setting that brings in absolutely nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan Thomas named his fictional village Llareggub, which reversed reads 'bugger all', British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas's 1954 radio drama is a great work set in the village of Llareggub.
